ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure has a central carbon skeleton, the central carbon is connected by single bonds to three terminal carbon groups, presenting a tert-butyl structure; the central carbon is also connected by a single bond to an oxygen atom labeled OH2, and a positive charge symbol in the figure indicates that this oxygen is protonated oxygen, namely OH2+. The curved arrows in the figure are not part of the molecular connectivity. Then reason: After ignoring the arrows, the molecular connectivity is (CH3)3C-OH2+. According to the method draft, choose one methyl as the starting point of the main chain and write it as CC; the central carbon additionally has two methyl branches, written as CC(C)(C); then connect the protonated oxygen, written as [OH2+]. Therefore the SMILES is CC(C)(C)[OH2+].

method.method_draft: First identify the non-arrow molecular skeleton in the image: the central carbon has four single bonds, three to methyl groups and one to a protonated oxygen labeled OH2+. Convert this connectivity to SMILES by choosing one methyl as the main chain start, writing the central carbon next with two methyl branches, and attaching the charged oxygen as [OH2+]. This gives CC(C)(C)[OH2+].
